thread.title: Hong Kong Bourse May Hand Back Monday

author: rttnews.com
title: Hong Kong Bourse May Hand Back Monday
text:
The Hong Kong stock market bounced higher again on Monday, one session after it had ended the three-day winning streak in which it had gathering more than 290 points or 1.1 percent. The Hang Seng Index now rests just above the 25,630-point plateau although it's expected to see renewed selling pressure on Tuesday.
The global forecast for the Asian markets is soft, with weakness expected among the technology stocks and oil companies. The European and U.S. markets were down and the Asian bourse are expected to follow suit.
The Hang Seng finished slightly higher on Monday following gains from the financials and mixed performances from the oil and insurance companies.
For the day, the index added 31/26 points or 0.12 percent to finish at 25,633.18 after trading between 25,505.33 and 25,765.96.
Among the actives, China Resources Power Holdings surged 5.63 percent, AAC Technologies plummeted 3.28 percent, Tencent Holdings plunged 3.08 percent, China Mengniu Dairy tumbled 1.84 percent, China Mobile soared 1.78 percent, CSPC Pharmaceutical spiked 1.64 percent, AIA Group jumped 1.60 percent, CNOOC climbed 1.48 percent, Hong Kong & China Gas advanced 1.08 percent, China Petroleum and Chemical (Sinopec) dropped 1.05 percent, Sands China skidded 0.79 percent, BOC Hong Kong collected 0.69 percent, Ping An Insurance shed 0.45 percent, Galaxy Entertainment lost 0.35 percent, China Life Insurance added 0.25 percent, New World Development fell 0.20 percent and Industrial and Commercial Bank of China was unchanged.
The lead from Wall Street is broadly negative as stocks moved extending losses from the previous session.

A sharp decline by shares of Apple (AAPL) and General Electric (GE) weighed on the markets, while concerns about the outlook for global economic growth and a continued increase in interest rates also contributed to the sell-off.
Light trading activity may have exaggerated the downward move, however, as government offices, the bond markets, and most banks were closed in observance of Veterans Day.
Crude oil shook off early gains on Monday to end lower for the 11th straight session on oversupply concerns. Crude oil futures for December, which rose to $61.28 earlier in the session, settled lower by $0.26 or 0.4 percent at $59.93 a barrel, the lowest settlement since February.
